Bug_Details: Calling Iterator.hasNext() is not supposed to have any side effects and hence should not change the iterator’s state. Iterator.next() advances the iterator by one item. So calling it inside Iterator.hasNext() breaks the hasNext() contract and will lead to unexpected behavior in production.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method. Inside the if condition, iterator.next() is called inside iterator.hasNext(), which breaks the hasNext() contract as it is not supposed to have any side effects.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method with a list that has only one element. This causes `iterator.next()` to be called inside `iterator.hasNext()`, which is against the contract and leads to an unexpected `NoSuchElementException` when we try to call `iterator.next()` again.
